subtype: Approach: running in panic through the lanes [Pitfall]
passage: From my uncle's shoe stall I saw a boy of about ten sprinting between the lanes, head twisting left and right. His mother, Dolma, I learned later, was running the opposite way, calling his name. The lanes bend, so each time one of them turned a corner the other had already gone through. Once he nearly hit a pole and I called, "Do you know your father's number?" He opened his mouth and only gasps came out. I can't tell what he was thinking; maybe he was too scared to think at all. In the end my uncle stepped into the middle of the lane and waved them both over. - Himani

qa.q: What happened when the narrator asked the boy for his father's number?
qa.a: He opened his mouth and only gasps came out.

qa.q: What might the boy have been feeling as he ran?
qa.a: Terrified, probably, since he was too scared to think and could not even say a number he knew.

qa.q: What could the boy try instead of running, and why?
qa.a: He could stop, breathe and ask a shopkeeper to call, because staying put lets his parents find him and calm lets him remember the number.

qa.q: How does the search look from Dolma's side?
qa.a: Dolma is frightened and calling his name, and because she also keeps moving, each turn takes her past him.

grounding: A child sprints through lanes in panic while the parents also move, so they keep missing each other.
